release_notes: Hotfix for yesterday's security instructions: the patch command we printed was broken. If you ran "apt upgrade 'php*'" from the v1.7.5 banner or notes, apt tried to install every php-named package in the Ubuntu archive, hit package conflicts and upgraded NOTHING — your PHP is still unpatched. The working command is: "apt update && apt install --only-upgrade 'php8.X-*'" (replace X with your branch, e.g. php8.5-*), then "systemctl restart php8.5-fpm nginx" (no apache2 — that error was ours too). The banner now prints exactly that, with your branch substituted. The advisory itself is unchanged: CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619 ("php2shell") are unauthenticated RCE bugs in PHP itself with a public exploit; fixed releases are 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35, and PHP 8.1 or older will never get one (re-run "sudo bash install.sh" to move to PHP 8.5). Distro builds may carry the fix backported under the old version number: apt changelog php-fpm | grep 109618.
